The exposure on the operative chain is real, not inert.
mitigants_held: Reputation-write authority is ROTATED off the leaked keys (current writer 0xb2426888, no private-key leak evidence) — so on-chain reputation writes are not forgeable via the historically-leaked keys.

Value at risk is TESTNET ETH only; mainnet keys are inert (CLAUDE.md: mainnet nonce 0).

attestor_signer_investigation_2026_08_17.question: Is the EIP-712 attestor key HYPERDAG_ATTESTOR_PRIVATE_KEY the leaked 0xf6eE1768, or a rotated key?

narrowed_by_observation.two_attestation_systems: ACTIVE public attestation (/api/v1/repid/verify + /api/v1/repid/:id/attest) uses ed25519 SIGNING_KEY_DEV — NOT the leaked EVM key. The EIP-712/EVM attestor (HYPERDAG_ATTESTOR_PRIVATE_KEY) is a separate system.
narrowed_by_observation.eip712_attestor_wiring: repIdAttestationService.generateAttestation() is called ONLY on the x402-inbound settlement path (src/routes/x402-inbound.ts:157); the attestation is returned transiently in the X-HYPERDAG-REPID-ATTESTATION response header AFTER an x402 payment settles. It is NOT persisted.
narrowed_by_observation.no_recoverable_artifact: reputation_attestations table holds 2 rows, both signing_address=0x0000...0000 and signature='signing_status=deferred' (placeholders from a different, deferred flow) — no real EIP-712 signature to recover a signer from.
narrowed_by_observation.fallback_removed: The hardcoded 0xf6eE fallback was removed 2026-07-31; repid-attestation.ts now REQUIRES HYPERDAG_ATTESTOR_PRIVATE_KEY or refuses to sign. So a rotation done at/after that date would be effective.
